meta.name: All Things ODD — brand tokens
meta.sourceOfTruth: The website's CSS is canonical for the web: src/styles/tokens.css and src/styles/typography.css. This file mirrors every value a non-web tool needs (decks, print, social, Figma, an AI agent). `npm run check:brand` fails the build if a mirrored web value drifts from the CSS.
meta.units: Web values are CSS strings exactly as written in the stylesheets. px values are at the default 16px root unless a width is named. Deck values are points on a 13.333 x 7.5 in (16:9) slide.

ink.role: The ground. The most common colour in 1,478 archive photographs (32.7% coverage): a rose-tinted near-black, never print black.

paper.role: The one light neutral. Figure on Ink; the ground of ODDspace and of inverse moments (menu, Ways to take part).

backstage.role: Raised surface on Ink: cards, bands, panels.

amber.role: Ember, the warm stage light. Creative / ODDfest. A wash or keyline on Ink; text only on Paper.

amberBright.role: Ember as text on Ink (4.62:1). The creative voice label; the heat colour on Ink.

signal.role: Signal, the lighting desk's cool blue. Business / ODDference. Washes, rules, form accents.

signalBright.role: Signal as text on Ink (4.83:1). The business voice label.

signalDeep.role: Signal as a fill under Paper text (4.79:1): consent and system buttons.

clay.role: Quiet warm neutral. Large text or decoration only (4.32:1 on Ink).

clayRead.role: Clay as small text on Ink (5.23:1): the legal line.

clayReadLight.role: Clay as small text on Paper (5.21:1).

indigo.role: Scrim tint under archive imagery. Never text, never a fill.

ultraviolet.role: The archive's rarest colour. A wash on ODDfest moments only, at most a 16% mix. Never a fill, never text.

opacityRamp.note: Figure over ground. Dark: Paper over Ink. Light: Ink over Paper. Tuned by measured contrast, not mirrored: Ink on Paper needs more opacity for the same ratio. Step names are historical; the values are what ship.

semantic.note: Roles, not colours. Each role is a CSS variable that already flips under .theme-light (ODDspace), so components never branch on theme. The CSS names predate the roles (--color-paper means 'figure', because Paper is the figure on the default ground) and are kept rather than aliased, so code has one vocabulary.

groundRaised.use: Cards, bands and panels one step off the page.

figure.use: Headlines, primary text, solid buttons, the mark.

figureMuted.use: Body copy under a headline; secondary text; captions.

figureQuiet.use: Eyebrows, labels, meta, the quiet premise of a two-tone headline. The lowest step allowed for text.

lineControl.use: Border of an outline button. Not for text.

ruleStrong.use: Rules that must read at a glance; the underline of a text link.

rule.use: Hairlines: section-head rules, grid lines, card borders, the nav edge.

heat.use: What anything pressable warms to on hover or press: links, rows, keylines of linked bands.

voiceCreative.use: The 'For creatives' label and creative-side accents.

voiceBusiness.use: The 'For business' label and business-side accents.

systemAction.use: Fill of consent and system buttons that are not brand CTAs.

legal.use: Footer legal line and fine print.

scrim.use: Over photographs under text. Always Ink, never #000: 45-82% at the text, 8-20% away from it.

contrast.note: WCAG 2.x ratios on the composited colour against its real ground. AA: 4.5 small text; 3.0 large text (24px+, or 18.66px+ bold) and UI edges.

pairs.ok: large text only; use signalDeep behind small text

rules: Ink or Paper is the ground. Nothing else is ever a page or slide background.
Accents are light, not paint: text, keylines, washes and heat. Never a large flat fill.
One accent per moment. Ember and Signal share a surface only where it is about both sides.
Creative before business: where both appear, Ember sits first (left or above).
No new colour without provenance in the archive study, recorded in tokens.css.

display.name: Forta
display.case: Unicase: lowercase is drawn as capitals, so every Forta setting reads as caps.
display.use: Statements: headlines, names, figures, navigation, rails.

body.name: Gabarito
body.use: Everything read or operated: paragraphs, labels, buttons, forms.

families.fallback: Where the fonts cannot be installed: Arial for Gabarito. Forta has no substitute; set the line as an image or wait for the font.

hero.use: The one dominant statement on a page or slide.

display.use: Page titles, major statements, headline figures.

heading.use: Section, card, column, list and FAQ titles.

body.use: Every sentence meant to be read, and every form field.

small.use: Labels, meta, dates, buttons, captions, helper text.

treatments.note: Twelve jobs, five sizes. Hierarchy inside a size comes from face, weight, colour, case, tracking and position, never from a sixth size.

display.detail: Monumental. One per page or slide.

h2.detail: Section title, centred over a hairline rule (.section-head).

h4.detail: Forta at the Body size (session titles, names on photo cards), or Gabarito 600 at the Body size for a run-in title on its own paragraph.

lead.detail: Body in figureStrong on a wider measure. Not a bigger size.

bodyLarge.detail: Deliberately absent. Use lead, or promote to heading.

navigation.detail: Forta at the Body size, 0.01em tracking, figure at 80%.

rules: Five sizes. Nothing on screen below 14px.
Forta never sets a paragraph. Past three lines it is Body.
Headlines are sentences and end with a full stop.
Premise, then point: a two-sentence headline sets the first sentence in figureQuiet and the second in figure.
Uppercase is typographic only (eyebrows, buttons). Never type in capitals; Forta capitalises for you.

content.use: A heading or intro to what it introduces (.flow).

group.use: One group to the next inside a section.

section.use: Between two sections; owned by layout.css.

breakpoints.note: Canonical layout breakpoints (px, not rem: they describe the viewport). A component may add a content breakpoint where its own content breaks, named in a comment, never to change a type size.

desktopScale.note: The root ramps 16px to 20px between 1024 and 1440px. Desktop widths are written in rem so they grow with it.

grid.mobile: 1 column for reading, 2-4 columns for hairline image mosaics
grid.hairlineGap: 1-2px: the ground showing through is the rule

rails.use: Fixed vertical tickers on product pages: lockup, product name, city, year.

none.use: Everything that holds content: photographs, cards, grids, bands, tables, ask boxes.

panel.use: Surfaces floating over the page: dropdown, consent, newsletter, bottom sheet. Nested corners: calc(var(--radius-panel) - inset).

pill.use: Things you act on or that label something small: buttons, tags, badges, status. The shape of the mark's lobes.

border.keyline: 2px solid heat: the one accent edge, on a band that is a link
border.strike: 2.5px figure, through the middle of a nav word on hover and for the current page

reveal.use: Scroll reveal: fade plus a 14px rise.

spring.use: A small overshoot for a physical object. Rare.

ambient.mosaic: Ken Burns pan and self-swap from the archive pool
ambient.steam: turbulence displacement on the hero and nav mark

rules: Every animation has a reduced-motion branch: it never attaches, or it becomes a still.
Animation never hides content: the hidden state exists only while the script that reveals it runs (html.reveal-js).
No scroll-jacking, no parallax on text, no counters that make a number wait.

grade.underText: add brightness(0.8-0.92) and an Ink scrim
grade.portraits: greyscale in speaker grids, full colour everywhere else

image.logosOfOthers: Monochrome in the figure colour (filter: brightness(0) invert(1) on Ink).
rules: Real ODD moments only: the archive, the venues, the people.
No stock photography, no generated people, no mock-ups presented as events.
Crop to the action: faces, hands, instruments, the crowd, not the empty stage.

mark.clearSpace: Half the mark's height on every side.

logo.icon: brand/logos/svg/odd-icon.svg: the Paper mark on an Ink tile, corner radius 24/128.
